wall.pageTitle: Can a reputation be sold this cheaply?
wall.lead1: $NATRO was sold on a name. The pitch was never really the token — it was the family behind it, and the trust a known surname is supposed to carry. Within 48 hours the price fell 98%, refunds were refused, and the evidence began to disappear.
wall.lead2: What remains is a question worth putting on the record: in an age when a reputation can be borrowed to raise money and discarded the moment the money is raised, how little is a name actually worth?
wall.pullquote: “The reputation hit lasts forever; the cash from a rug doesn’t.” — from the $NATRO website’s own FAQ.
wall.inviteLead: If the $NATRO launch — or the family name used to sell it — cost you money, time, or trust, describe what happened in your own words. Comments are read and moderated before they appear. Keep to what you experienced and can stand behind.

privacy.title: Privacy & cookies
privacy.lead: This page describes what data the case file collects, why, and how to opt out.
privacy.what_p1: If you accept analytics, two tools run. Google Analytics 4 records aggregated, anonymised usage data — which pages you visit, time on page, approximate country, device class; we pass anonymize_ip=true so your IP is truncated before storage. Microsoft Clarity records aggregated interaction analytics — clicks, scrolls, and heatmaps, plus session replays in which text input is masked by default — to show how the file is actually read.
privacy.what_p2: If you decline, no analytics cookies are written. Google Analytics stays loaded under Consent Mode v2 in a denied state, so nothing is reported to Google. Microsoft Clarity stays in its cookieless mode and is never granted consent, so it writes no cookies and does not stitch your visits together.
privacy.what_p3: Independently of your choice, the site uses a cookieless, privacy-first visit counter (Ahrefs Web Analytics) that sets no cookies and collects no personal data, so it needs no consent.
privacy.no_p1: No advertising, marketing, or personalisation cookies. No ad networks, no cross-site profiling, and no sale of data — beyond the analytics tools described above, nothing else tracks you here.
privacy.user_p1: If you create an account to submit a reader story, we store your email, username, optional display name, and your submission. This data is held in our own database, never sold or shared. You can request deletion any time by contacting the editor.
privacy.change_p1: Clear this site's data in your browser to see the consent banner again. Or contact the editor.
